candidate.title: MAB-seq
candidate.scope: The assigned poster row labelled MAB-seq: M.SssI methylase-assisted bisulfite sequencing to map 5fC/5caC, including its explicitly depicted Control and M.SssI branches and their separate bisulfite/PCR DNA products. The complete supplied image was inspected: the partial caMAB-seq row above, fCAB-Seq row, RRMAB-seq row below, and N3-5GMC chemical icon at right are neighboring catalogue context, not connected steps or alternative targets of this MAB-seq row. The matching collection page is headed MAB-seq and describes the same two-path architecture. This is the depicted core assay, not a complete library-preparation implementation; the shared terminal DNA glyph does not establish pooling, and sequencing is interpreted from text without adding an unshown operation.

states.label: Genomic DNA containing unmodified and modified cytosines
features: The representative input panel orders the depicted cytosine classes as C, 5mC, 5hmC, 5fC and 5caC; these are modification-class examples rather than an asserted literal genomic sequence.
The biological targets are 5-formylcytosine (5fC) and 5-carboxylcytosine (5caC) in DNA. The informative protection/readout operates at CpG sites.

Results, Experimental strategy and validation of MAB-seq, [b00008]
evidence.quote: In standard BS-seq, C/5fC/5caC react with sodium bisulfite and are efficiently deaminated to uracil (C/5fC) or 5caU (5caC), both of which are sequenced as thymine (T), whereas 5mC and 5hmC are resistant to this chemical conversion and sequenced as C (Fig. 1a).

states.label: MAB-seq bisulfite-PCR DNA product: C C C T T
features: At protected CpG sites, original C / 5mC / 5hmC are represented as C, while 5fC / 5caC are represented as T.

The amplified DNA sequence is the readout carrier: a T at an interrogated reference CpG cytosine contributes to the combined 5fC/5caC signal; it cannot identify which of those two modifications was present. C does not distinguish original C from 5mC or 5hmC. The proportion T/(T+C) is the raw combined-modification signal before accounting for background.

The ideal C/T code depends on effective methylation and bisulfite conversion. Incomplete M.SssI methylation can create background T and overestimate target abundance; Non-CpG unmodified C is not reliably protected and can also yield T.

evidence.quote: For a CpG site, if we name the number of T reads as NT and the number of C reads as NC, 5fC+5caC level (MAB-seq raw signal before background subtraction) can be calculated as NT/(NT+NC). Because conversion of unmodified C to 5mC by M.sssI cannot reach 100%, some T reads may come from incomplete methylation rather than real 5fC/5caC, leading to an overestimation of 5fC/5caC level.

operations.label: M.SssI
operations.description: M.SssI acts on starting genomic DNA to convert originally unmodified cytosines within CpG dinucleotides to 5mC. The treated output retains the pre-existing modified classes, including the target 5fC and 5caC.
operations.mechanism: CpG-directed cytosine methylation protects originally unmodified C from subsequent bisulfite deamination. M.SssI is an enzyme reagent acting on DNA, not a material product or readout carrier.
operations.information_effect: Installs a protective modification on background CpG C so that subsequent T representation can identify the combined 5fC/5caC class. Original C and pre-existing 5mC become indistinguishable by this readout.

operations.label: Bisulfite treatment / PCR amplification
operations.description: Processes the control DNA independently: bisulfite deaminates C and 5fC to uracil and 5caC to 5caU; PCR produces a DNA sequence representation with T at those original positions. Original 5mC and 5hmC positions are represented as C, giving the depicted T C C T T product.
operations.mechanism: The two stacked source captions are retained as one local bisulfite-then-PCR block. The primary text resolves the chemical intermediate as uracil for C/5fC and 5caU for 5caC; both are read as T.
operations.information_effect: The control DNA product groups C, 5fC and 5caC into the T class and 5mC/5hmC into the C class. It does not directly identify the oxidized targets.

operations.description: Processes M.SssI-treated DNA independently: protected CpG C and pre-existing 5mC/5hmC retain C representation, while target 5fC and 5caC undergo bisulfite conversion and become T in the amplified DNA product. The depicted output is C C C T T.

method_scopes.rationale: The single assigned row explicitly labels MAB-seq and contains both a Control comparison and an M.SssI path. Control denotes the route bypassing M.SssI, not an additional transformation or a negative biological control. Both downstream blocks are local instances with branch-specific input history and output. The five modification classes and separate ideal C/T patterns define the readout. The collection heading/caption and primary full-text Results resolve this as M.SssI-based mapping of 5fC/5caC at CpGs. Neighboring rows have separate method names and separate arrow routes; RRMAB restriction digestion/adaptor addition and fCAB chemical blocking are not part of this target row.
